why: All three checks pass and none of the refutation routes applies. (1) VERBATIM: curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/keybindings.md line 9 reads in full 'Claude Code supports customizable keyboard shortcuts. Run `/keybindings` to create or open your configuration file at `~/.claude/keybindings.json`.' The claimed sentence is the second half, word for word; the first half does not reverse it. The page is row 120 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a valid Claude contract source. (2) CITED LINES: apps/electron/src/renderer/actions/registry.tsx:23 is exactly '// User hotkey overrides (future: load from config)', :24 the interface field, :31 'const userOverrides = useRef<Map<ActionId, string | null>>(new Map())', :61-62 the getHotkey read, :116 the context-value read. `grep -rn -a userOverrides` over all .ts/.tsx returns those five hits and nothing else — the map is never written. apps/electron/src/renderer/actions/types.ts:1 is the four-value ActionScope. slash-command-menu.tsx:17 SlashCommandId has no 'keybindings'. (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier: no keybindings.json loader exists anywhere (`grep -rn -a 'keybindings.json|loadKeybindings|readKeybindings'` over apps+packages = 0 hits); no hotkey key in packages/shared/src/config; the main-process menu accelerators in apps/electron/src/main/menu.ts are hardcoded literals, not a second override path; KeyboardShortcutsDialog.tsx is a read-only reference that renders actionsByCategory plus static component lists, with no editing or persistence. So getHotkey always returns actions[id].defaultHotkey and a user cannot rebind anything by any route. Not an owner decision: keybindings is not among the nine dated entries in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3. Not a declared product difference either — it is unrelated to the dropped Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows, the corporate gateway, or the rename. The closest recorded judgement is 2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1720, which lists keybindings under 'Minor, no row, listed for completeness' — that triages the gap as low priority, it does not deny it; and 2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:113 already marks the page yellow. Three wording corrections are needed but none reverses the verdict, see correctedState.
correctedState: CONFIRMED with three corrections to the wording. (a) 'no `namespace:action` vocabulary' is misleading: a namespaced action vocabulary does exist, it uses a dot instead of a colon — apps/electron/src/renderer/actions/definitions.ts declares 27 ids of the form `app.newChat`, `nav.focusChat`, `view.toggleSidebar`, `navigator.selectAll`, `panel.focusNext`, `chat.stopProcessing`. What is absent is the file-level vocabulary and the colon spelling, not the concept. (b) 'no `null`-to-unbind' is imprecise: the registry's data model already treats null as unbound — types.ts:7 `defaultHotkey: string | null  // null = no default hotkey`, registry.tsx:31 `Map<ActionId, string | null>`, :61-62 `?? null`, and the keydown loop at :84 does `if (!hotkey || !matchesHotkey(...)) continue`. An override of null would unbind correctly today; there is simply no file to write one in. (c) The evidence names the wrong mechanism for contexts. `ActionScope` (types.ts:1) is declared-but-never-read metadata — only three definitions set it (definitions.ts:158, :166, :197) and no code reads `.scope`. The live context gate is the `when` clause on ActionDefinition, evaluated by `evaluateWhen()` in apps/electron/src/renderer/actions/keybinding-context.ts against a six-key `KeybindingContext` (inputFocus, hasSelection, chatFocus, navigatorFocus, sidebarFocus, menuOpen). The comparison to Claude's 19 contexts should be made against those six, not against ActionScope's four — the mismatch holds either way. Scope note worth recording alongside the row: the Claude page is terminal-TUI-scoped (tmux and GNU screen prefix conflicts, `app:redraw` 'Force terminal redraw', Ctrl+M 'Identical to Enter in terminals', vim-mode interaction, a `Scroll` fullscreen context), and apps/cli has no interactive TUI at all (no setRawMode/readline/keypress hits), so the only comparable surface here is the Electron renderer and the 19 contexts do not map one-to-one. The user-facing capability the page promises — customize shortcuts through a config file, discoverable via a slash command — is nonetheless entirely absent, and registry.tsx:23 self-declares it as future work.
